title: Innate sensor responses set a supra-unitary threshold for viral replication
title_zh: 固有传感器反应为病毒复制设定超单位阈值
abstract: Cells resist viral infection by triggering rapid and sensitive innate immune responses, initiated by cytoplasmic viral sensor proteins (CyVSP), retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I), melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA-5), and protein kinase R (PKR). Our single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary viral genome input, significantly more than one, which we define as the virion input threshold for replication (VITREP). This threshold varies depending on viruses and cell types, independently of viral protein synthesis. Through mathematical modeling and experimental testing, we uncover that supra-unitary viral genome quantities activate negative feedback regulators (NFR) of CyVSP, including death-associated protein kinase 1 (DAPK1), Rio kinase 3 (RIOK3), and protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit alpha (PPP2R2A), that suppress innate immune responses and allow replication. We validate key predictions of our model, namely that downregulating NFR reduces replication, whereas upregulating NFR or coinfecting cells promotes replication. Together, these findings reveal a fundamental mechanism governing viral infectivity and tissue tropism.
abstract_zh: 细胞通过触发快速且敏感的固有免疫反应来抵抗病毒感染，该反应由胞质病毒传感蛋白（CyVSP）启动，包括抗感染基因I（RIG-I）、melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5（MDA-5）和蛋白激酶R（PKR）。我们的单细胞分析显示，病毒复制需要超单位的病毒基因组输入，即远超一个病毒基因组，我们将其定义为病毒输入复制阈值（VITREP）。该阈值因病毒类型和细胞类型而异，且独立于病毒蛋白合成。通过数学建模和实验测试，我们发现超单位的病毒基因组数量激活了CyVSP的负反馈调节因子（NFR），包括死亡相关蛋白激酶1（DAPK1）、Rio激酶3（RIOK3）和蛋白磷酸酶2调节亚基α（PPP2R2A），从而抑制固有免疫反应并允许复制。我们验证了模型的关键预测，即下调NFR会减少复制，而上调NFR或共感染细胞则促进复制。总之，这些发现揭示了病毒感染性和组织特异性的基本调控机制。
